sources.statement: The skill is shipped to downstream repositories whose build and test commands it cannot know; .amigos/config.json carries no test command and the request does not say how one is discovered.

Responsibility 5 says 'Run tests and evals', but this repository contains no eval harness: there is no evals/ directory, no grader runner, and no amigos export-evals command. README lists eval export under Phase 7 / STORY-008, two milestones away. Only the 'run tests' half of that step can be performed.

Every governed edit /implement makes is subject to the gate's active-story resolution (AMIGOS_STORY, .amigos/ACTIVE, branch name). The ticket does not say that /implement makes its story resolvable. This checkout is currently on a detached HEAD, where branch resolution yields nothing and the first Write is refused.

The ticket lists "run tests and evals", but no eval corpus, golden task or grader exists and evals are assigned to Phase 7 (STORY-008), so whether this milestone runs anything beyond the repository's own test suite is unsettled.

The request does not say whether this story includes actually running /implement against a real story, or whether shipping the skill is the whole deliverable — v0.4 deliberately did not close until its dogfooding run produced a number.

The request does not say whether /implement performs git operations — creating the branch that lets the gate resolve the story, staging, committing — or assumes a resolvable active story already exists in the environment.
Whether a single /implement run must complete a whole story, and what happens when it cannot — resumption, partial delivery, a second run over the same contract — is not addressed.

The ticket does not settle whether v0.5 ships only a prompt (skills/implement/SKILL.md plus tests holding it to the code, the shape v0.3 and v0.4 used) or also new deterministic support: a contract-immutability diff, a scope-expansion check, a test-command config key, a lifecycle state. The two readings differ by a schema change and several new CLI surfaces, and the second is plausibly more than one change.

The ticket does not settle whether /implement is SKILL.md text only or also ships code (a coverage report, a contract-immutability check, a new amigos subcommand). That decision changes what can be judged from outside: prompt-only delivery leaves every scenario here to review rather than to a test.

Declaring contract_change on discovering a contract problem withholds readiness, after which the gate refuses the partially written code; the request does not say whether that partial work is reverted, left in place, or committed before the declaration.

The gate exempts '.amigos/**', so an implementation agent can edit acceptance.feature and the PreToolUse hook will permit it. 'The implementation skill must not modify acceptance criteria' is therefore prompt text only. dor.json.contract_hash is recorded as the baseline but nothing diffs against it anywhere in src/, and docs/versions/v0.2-repository-gate/gap-analysis.md assigns that diffing to v0.6.

'The implementation skill must not modify acceptance criteria' has no mechanical backing at v0.5: .amigos/** is exempt in .amigos/config.json, so the repository gate and the PreToolUse hook both permit an implementation agent to edit acceptance.feature. The only observable trace of a violation is hash drift against dor.json's contract_hash, and nothing currently compares them after a run.

Whether /implement ships any mechanical protection against editing acceptance.feature, or only the stated rule, is unsettled: README Phase 6 and STORY-007's Out of Scope both assign contract immutability to a later milestone, yet the gate exempts .amigos/** so nothing refuses the edit today.

The command signature is a story id alone, and the request does not say what /implement does when the invoking user adds instructions beyond the contract, which is the main path by which scope re-enters after the gate has been satisfied.

Whether an implemented story is recorded anywhere is unsettled: the lifecycle has no declared state between ready and the next contract change, so nothing distinguishes a ready story that has been built from one that has not.

Packaging beyond skills/implement/SKILL.md is unsettled: README section 19 also names a CLAUDE.md repository rule this checkout does not contain, and section 20 names a Codex mirror the roadmap defers.

'Check for scope expansion' names no basis of comparison. Candidates in this system are the acceptance scenarios, the 'Relevant Components' list in constraints.md, and the story's Out of Scope entries; the ticket picks none, so the check has no pass or fail.

tests/test_dogfooding.py enumerates this repository's story ids and excludes STORY-006, so closing this milestone changes a governed test file as a side effect, and the same happens for whichever story /implement is first used on.

tests/test_dogfooding.py enumerates STORY_IDS as a literal tuple that omits STORY-006, so a newly ready story is not automatically held to the self-hosting invariant. Closeout also requires 'amigos status' to exit 0, which it cannot while STORY-006 declares amigos_running or fails a check.
"Establish a baseline where useful" reads either as running the existing suite before any change or as requiring the new tests to fail first, and the two produce different observable evidence.

'Translate relevant Then clauses into tests' leaves 'relevant' undefined, and this repository's own contracts contain Then clauses no unit test can judge - for example STORY-004's 'the skill reports the remaining findings'. Two readers would disagree about which clauses must become tests and what happens to the ones that cannot.

Nothing states what /implement does with a Then clause it cannot express as an automated test — several clauses in this repository's own contracts assert on prompt text or on a file's absence — nor whether such a clause blocks the run or is reported and skipped.

The request covers only the ready and not-ready cases; it says nothing about a story id that does not exist, or a contract the validator cannot read at all (exit code 2) as distinct from one evaluated and found not ready.

No scenario covers /implement invoked against a story that is not ready, does not exist, or is structurally unusable (dor.evaluate raises StructuralError and writes no dor.json, exit code 2). The refusal is the load-bearing behaviour of the skill and is the case most likely to be implemented by accident.

The milestone's exit criterion — "moves from a ready contract to verified implementation without redefining the requirement" — names no evidence: it does not say which story demonstrates it, what counts as "verified", or what artefact shows the requirement was not redefined.

The exit criterion 'moves from a ready contract to verified implementation without redefining the requirement' names no artifact. Nothing says what a reviewer inspects to decide the requirement was not redefined, so two reviewers can judge the same run differently. A decidable form exists in this repository already: the sha256 of each contract input file still equals the hash dor.json recorded before the run.

README section 14 tells /implement to read dor.json for "ready": true, while docs/component-design/gate.md states a committed dor.json is a record and never an authority because the gated agent can write it; the contract must settle which rule /implement follows.

There is no lifecycle state meaning 'implementation in progress'. story.DECLARABLE_STATES is ('draft', 'amigos_running', 'contract_change') and state.schema.json pins a closed enum with additionalProperties false, in both the top level and each history entry. Recording an implementation run in the lifecycle is a schema change touching story.py, dor.py, the schema, README section 5 and docs/component-design/contract-protocol.md - and any state added must not withhold readiness, or the gate would refuse the very writes the run is making.

Responsibility 6, 'Check for scope expansion', has no mechanism in this system. Nothing compares a code diff against intent.md's In Scope and Out of Scope lists, and no CLI subcommand computes it (build_parser exposes init, create, check, lint, status, gate, state, findings, hooks). As written the check is a model's self-assessment, which is the thing this project replaces elsewhere with code.

'Run tests and evals' names evals, which do not exist in this repository; eval export is phase 7 (v0.7) and 'amigos export-evals' is listed as a potential later command. The clause cannot be satisfied as written at v0.5, and an agent told to run evals will either invent one or quietly drop the step.

On a contract conflict the ticket shows '/implement -> contract_change -> /amigos' without saying who acts. Both readings are buildable: /implement runs 'amigos state --set contract_change' and stops for a human, or it invokes /amigos itself. The second lets one session both discover a conflict and rewrite the criterion it conflicted with.

"Check for scope expansion" does not say what the change is compared against — constraints.md's Relevant Components, intent.md's Out of Scope, or the diff alone — nor whether a detected expansion stops the run or is only reported.

"Report discrepancies" does not say where the report goes; /amigos is forbidden from writing commentary into the story directory and puts its run evidence in .amigos/runs/, so whether an implement run leaves any durable record or only speaks in chat is undecided.

"Implement the minimum required behavior" has no stated arbiter: minimal against the acceptance scenarios and minimal against intent.md's In Scope can differ, and nothing says which governs when they do.

The ticket says the skill checks that dor.json contains 'ready': true. gate.py deliberately does the opposite: it recomputes readiness from the contract files on every call because a committed dor.json 'may be stale, and it is writable by the agent being gated'. A skill that trusts the file would accept a verdict the gate rejects, or authorise implementation from a hand-edited record.

Declaring contract_change withholds readiness immediately, so the gate and the pre-commit hook then refuse every governed write - including committing the partial implementation already in the working tree. The ticket's escalation path does not say whether the skill declares contract_change on discovery, after reporting, or only once the working tree is clean, and the three differ in whether work in progress can be saved.

README section 14's "business code" is never reconciled with the gate's "governed files", so whether /implement may write exempt paths such as docs/ while a story is not ready is open to two readings.

sources.statement: README section 14 says dor.json 'must contain ready: true' before business code changes; README section 18 says a committed dor.json is a record and never an authority because it is writable by the agent being gated. Two careful readers get two different preconditions for /implement, and one of them lets an agent authorise itself by editing a file.

keys.target_section: scenario: a ready contract reaches verified implementation

sources.target_section: Scenario: A ready contract reaches verified implementation
sources.statement: The ticket names no output for a run. Everything a reviewer would check afterwards - which scenario each test covers, which files changed and why, which scenarios remain unsatisfied - is only observable if the run leaves a report, and the ticket neither requires one nor says where it goes. /amigos settled the equivalent question by naming .amigos/runs/ as evidence outside the story directory.

keys.target_section: scenario: a test for absent behaviour fails before the source changes

sources.target_section: Scenario: A test for absent behaviour fails before the source changes
sources.statement: 'Establish a baseline where useful' gives no rule for when a baseline is required. The case it exists for is exactly the case an agent will judge as not useful: a test written after the code, which passes on the first run and therefore proves nothing about intent.

keys.target_section: scenario: a then no test can observe is named rather than dropped

sources.target_section: Scenario: A Then no test can observe is named rather than dropped
sources.statement: 'Translate relevant Then clauses into tests' defines neither 'relevant' nor what happens to a Then no test in this repository can observe. STORY-005's contract contains such clauses ('no agent's prompt contains another agent's output'), so the first dogfooding target already carries the failure mode: silently skip the hard clauses and report the contract as verified.

keys.target_section: scenario: an unsatisfied scenario is reported rather than made green

sources.target_section: Scenario: An unsatisfied scenario is reported rather than made green
sources.statement: The ticket has no failure mode for a run that cannot finish: tests still failing, a behaviour that turns out to be infeasible, budget exhausted. Nothing says whether partial code stays, whether the run reports success, or what state.json declares. The v0.4 notes record a run terminated by a session rate limit, so this is not hypothetical.

keys.target_section: scenario: the run takes no privileged path around the gate

sources.target_section: Scenario: The run takes no privileged path around the gate
sources.statement: The ticket lists no prohibition on the obvious escapes from a refusal: editing .claude/settings.json, uninstalling the pre-commit hook, or committing with --no-verify. README section 31 forbids a privileged path, but a skill that is never told this will find the escape faster than the fix.

'The project moves from a ready contract to verified implementation without redefining the requirement' names no artifact anyone can inspect. Without a stated observable - for example that the four contract files' hashes match dor.json.contract_hash before and after, and that the suite passes - no scenario can pass or fail this criterion.

The exit criterion requires moving from a ready contract to verified implementation, but /implement cannot implement STORY-006 - the skill would have to exist first. STORY-001 to STORY-005 and STORY-007 are already implemented, so the story that demonstrates the criterion does not exist yet and the ticket does not name it.

'Establish a baseline where useful' names no criterion for 'useful' and no artifact. Nothing in the repository defines what a baseline is or where it would be recorded, so the step is entirely the implementer's judgement and leaves no trace a reviewer could check.

Nothing in the protocol names how a repository runs its tests. .amigos/config.json carries stories_dir, lint, dor and gate only, and config.py reads no other key. 'Run tests' resolves to 'python -m pytest -q' here by convention in docs/development-workflow.md, and to nothing at all in a downstream repository.

Writes made through Bash are not gated - docs/component-design/gate.md records this hole as deferred 'to be decided on evidence'. /implement is the first skill that needs Bash (to run tests), so it is the first consumer for which the gate's coverage is materially weaker than for a drafting agent.

docs/versions/v0.4-independent-subagents/implementation-notes.md records that skills are snapshotted when a session registers them, so a skill edited mid-session serves its old text. The session that writes skills/implement/SKILL.md is therefore unlikely to be the session that can invoke it, which constrains how this milestone can demonstrate itself.

v0.5 is judged by running /implement on Amigos Skills itself, and the v0.4 implementation notes record two environment facts that break that self-run: an agent type created in a session is not addressable in that session, and an edited SKILL.md serves its pre-edit text until something re-registers it. A milestone whose evidence is a self-run inherits both.
